pagina.dati.testo: The demo stores your visit history and the first battery reading in your browser, so it recognizes you on your next visit. This data never leaves the browser.
pagina.dati.fatto: Data deleted: on your next visit the demo will see you as new. Your chosen language and time zone stay.
errore.raccolta: Error while collecting the data. Try reloading the page.
avviso.testo: Everything below was read as soon as you opened the page, without asking you anything and without cookies. Put together, these data form a fingerprint that can recognize you from one visit to the next. The values marked with (*) make up your ID.
ritratto.nota: The page draws these sentences from the data below, as whoever collects them would. Move the mouse or scroll the page: the portrait updates.
ritratto.schermoDue: a {risoluzione} pixel screen plus a second monitor
ritratto.rete: You connect from the {fornitore} network, around {posizione}, without a VPN.
ritratto.reteVpn: You probably use a VPN: the IP belongs to {fornitore}, around {posizione}.
ritratto.reteFusoFalsato: The browser time zone is faked, as Tor and hardened Firefox do; the IP belongs to {fornitore}, around {posizione}.
ritratto.tastiera: Your keyboard layout is {tastiera} and the browser is set to {lingua}.
ritratto.estensioni: Among your browser extensions there are {elenco}.
ritratto.visite: This page has already seen you {n} times, the first on {data}.
ritratto.primaVisita: This is the first time this page sees you: on your next visit it will recognize you, even without cookies.
esclusi.titolo: Values left out of the calculation
esclusi.testo: These values look spoofed or too generic, so they do not count towards the uniqueness estimate.
gruppo.rete: Where you are and how you connect
valore.senzaBatteria: No battery, or full and plugged in
valore.rumorePresente: Present: the browser alters the sound to avoid being recognised
valore.vpnNessunIndizio: No clue: home or mobile network, and the same time as the browser's time zone
valore.vpnDatacenter: Likely: the IP belongs to a data centre, not to a home or mobile provider
valore.vpnProbabile: Likely: the browser's time zone does not show the same time as the IP's
valore.fusoFalsato: Spoofed time zone: the browser declares UTC, as Tor and Firefox with resistFingerprinting do
valore.formatiAltraLingua: No: the formats follow another language
sezione.visite.nota: Nine browser and hardware values, marked with (*), summed up in a code: your ID. It is not a cookie: the page computes it again at every visit, so deleting cookies does not change it. The visit history here stays in your browser, to show it to you; a real tracker would keep it on its server, and clearing the site data would not help.
sezione.visite.tag: Permission: no · External services: none · Saved in your browser
sezione.unicita.nota: For each value of the ID we estimate how many variants exist (the bits of entropy) and add them up. It is an upper bound: the values are not independent (graphics card, canvas and WebGL go together), so the real uniqueness is lower. On real people: 83.6% unique browsers out of 470 thousand (EFF, 2010), 33.6% out of 2 million (Gómez-Boix et al., 2018).
sezione.ip.nota: Your public address, asked of ipify; ipwho.is derives the network provider and, roughly, the city from it. WebRTC, the technology behind video calls, also asks a Google server for the address and with some VPNs reveals the real one. Browsers now hide the addresses of your home network. The IP's network is compared with a public list of data centre networks (bad-asn-list): VPNs and proxies usually exit from there.
sezione.ip.tag: Permission: no · External services: ipify, ipwho.is, Google STUN
sezione.fuso.nota: The time zone set in the system and that of the IP's location: if they do not show the same time it is a clue of a VPN or proxy, shown in IP and connection. Someone travelling without changing the clock gives the same result.
sezione.tastiera.nota: The key layout (Chrome and Edge only) and the way dates and numbers are written reveal the country better than the browser language, which often stays English.
sezione.reteDichiarata.nota: The connection type the browser tells websites. Chrome rounds the values and stops at 10 Mbps, precisely so that they do not become a fingerprint: the next section measures the real one.
sezione.reteMisurata.nota: The page downloads a file of random data from the site itself, for 3 seconds or up to 10 MB, and measures speed and response time: enough to tell fiber, mobile network and slow Wi-Fi apart.
sezione.reteMisurata.tag: Permission: no · External services: none · Up to 10 MB of data
sezione.browser.nota: What the browser declares to every site. For years the user agent has given generic values, but the languages, in the order you chose, remain very personal. Paradoxically, Do Not Track makes you more recognizable: few people turn it on.
sezione.clientHints.nota: Chrome and Edge give any page that asks the exact system version (it tells Windows 10 from 11), the phone model and the processor architecture.
sezione.hardware.nota: Resolution, pixel density, number of processor cores, touch points and Bluetooth presence: together they narrow down the device model a lot.
sezione.schermi.nota: From the difference between the screen and the free area one can tell where the taskbar is and how tall it is. The browser also says whether there is a second monitor.
sezione.schedaVideo.nota: WebGPU and WebGL reveal the maker and family of the graphics card, even when the name is hidden. The technical limits change from one model to another and from one driver to another.
sezione.batteria.nota: Chrome and Edge tell the level and charging state. The page keeps the first reading: two visits close in time with the same percentage can be linked even without cookies. A computer without a battery answers like a laptop at 100% and plugged in.
sezione.batteria.tag: Permission: no · External services: none · Saved in your browser
sezione.multimedia.nota: Which kinds of device there are: camera, microphone, speakers. Without permission the browser shows at most one per kind, without a name; if you gave this site permission in the past, it lists them all. Virtual devices from video software count too, and so do devices muted with their button: the browser sees they are connected, not that they work. The permission card further down shows the names.
sezione.periferiche.nota: No permission, just a gesture of yours: move the mouse, scroll the page, press a controller button or tap with the pen. From the rhythm of the movements the page tells a gaming mouse from a touchpad, which probably means a laptop; from a controller it reads name and model codes.
sezione.periferiche.attesaController: Press a controller button, if you have one
sezione.periferiche.attesaMouse: Move the mouse for a few seconds
sezione.periferiche.attesaPenna: Tap the page with the pen, if you have one
sezione.periferiche.mouseGioco: About {hz} readings per second: gaming mouse
sezione.periferiche.mouseNormale: About {hz} readings per second: regular mouse or touchpad
sezione.periferiche.touchpad: Smooth scrolling: touchpad, probably a laptop
sezione.periferiche.pennaSi: Yes: graphics tablet or screen with pen
sezione.sensori.nota: Which sensor interfaces the browser offers. It does not say whether the device really has the sensors: it is a hint about browser and system.
sezione.canvas.nota: The page draws a text you do not see and generates a sound you do not hear. The result changes slightly between graphics cards, drivers, systems and browsers, enough to tell them apart. WebGL also gives the name of the graphics card. Some browsers, such as Brave and Safari, add a tiny noise to the audio to blur the fingerprint: the page notices it with a sound whose result it already knows, and this defence too becomes a fact about you.
sezione.font.nota: The page measures the width of a text written with 48 different fonts: the installed ones change the measurement. The list reveals the system and software such as Office.
sezione.voci.nota: The voices for reading aloud depend on the system and on the languages you installed.
sezione.calcoli.nota: The same math functions give different results in the last digits depending on browser and system. The most recent emoji the system can draw tell how up to date it is.
sezione.preferenze.nota: Dark theme, reduced motion, contrast and other settings, including accessibility ones: few people use them, so they are very distinctive.
sezione.spazio.nota: The space granted to the site used to reveal the size of the disk and incognito mode. Today Chrome gives a fixed 10 GB in both cases, and that too tells which browser you use.
sezione.pubblicita.nota: The page inserts a fake ad banner and tries to load a script with an ad-like name. If the banner disappears or the script does not arrive, an extension such as uBlock Origin or Brave's protection blocked them. People who block ads are a minority, and this too sets you apart. A block in the network, such as Pi-hole, is not visible here: everything comes from the site itself, not from ad servers.
sezione.estensioni.nota: Many extensions can be recognized by any page. Cryptocurrency wallets announce themselves to whoever asks, developer tools and some extensions leave marks on the page. On Chrome and Edge the page also tries to read an internal file of every extension on a list: it answers only if the extension is there. LinkedIn does this with over 6,000 extensions. A wallet says you own cryptocurrency, something scammers are interested in too.
sezione.comportamento.nota: For 10 seconds the page counts mouse movements, clicks, scrolls and key presses. The way you move the mouse and type is as personal as a signature; here only counts and average speed are shown.
permessi.intro: These analyses ask for a permission: the browser shows a request and you can refuse. Open a card and press the button.
permessi.geo.testo: It reveals your position with an accuracy down to a few meters: it can be used to follow your movements and to find your home or workplace. The coordinates go to Nominatim (OpenStreetMap) to turn them into an address.
permessi.media.testo: It shows the exact names of the connected cameras, microphones and speakers: precise models, useful for a finer fingerprint.
permessi.media.tag: Permission: camera and microphone · External services: none
permessi.sensori.testo: It follows in real time how you move and tilt the device: it can reveal personal habits, such as the way you hold your phone. On a computer without sensors no data arrives.
permessi.sensori.tag: Permission: only on iPhone and iPad · External services: none
permessi.schermo.testo: It shows that a site can see everything you share: a whole screen, a window or a tab, as long as sharing stays on.
permessi.schermo.tag: Permission: screen sharing · External services: none
permessi.appunti.testo: It reads the text you copied last, in any program: it can be an address, a private message or a password just copied from your password manager.
permessi.periferiche.testo: The browser opens the list of connected or nearby devices and the page sees only the one you choose. From a USB device it reads name, maker, serial number and firmware: the serial number is the same on every site, and the permission stays, so on the next visit the site finds it again without asking. From a Bluetooth device it reads the name, which often contains the owner's, and, if the device allows it, battery, maker and model.
permessi.periferiche.tag: Permission: choice of a device · External services: none
permessi.periferiche.nonSupportate: Not supported by this browser: they work only with Chrome, Edge and Opera, on computers and Android.
permessi.nota.testo: These demos show what today's browsers can do. A malicious site can ask for the same permissions with a pretext: grant them only to sites you trust.
permessi.geo.indirizzoNonDisponibile: Could not look up the address (service temporarily unavailable)
permessi.media.nessunoTesto: The system did not detect any camera or microphone.
permessi.appunti.vuoti: The clipboard is empty or contains only an image.
permessi.periferiche.usbPrecedenti: USB devices granted on a previous visit: the site sees them without asking
permessi.periferiche.usbResta: The permission stays: on the next visit the site will see these devices without asking.
permessi.periferiche.nessunBluetooth: No device chosen, or Bluetooth is off.
permessi.periferiche.nonRisponde: The device gave no other data: many do not allow it.
permessi.schermo.soloComputer: Screen sharing not supported on this device (computers only)
permessi.schermo.avviso: You are sharing your screen. Everything visible can be recorded.
